name: Nuclear Engineering
boundaries: Nuclear Engineering: fundamental discoveries and enabling technologies within this field. Include cross-field consequences where the central advance belongs to this field; exclude routine incremental optimization. Use the historical breakthroughs in the prompt to calibrate revolutionary impact.

original_dispositions.reason: Reframed around demonstrated, service-relevant durability rather than complete immunity or a universal dose and lifetime.
The potential advantage of a substantially lower-neutron fuel cycle is distinct, but zero neutrons and zero activation are not assumed. Also overlaps NUC-01.

original_dispositions.original_title: Complete in-situ transmutation of all long-lived waste
original_dispositions.reason: Covered in part by NUC-03. The potentially transformative actinide-recycling concept is retained; complete conversion of every waste isotope, no secondary streams, and elimination of repositories are unsupported and not added as a separate concept.
Reframed as broad, demonstrable passive safety within defined conditions, with residual risk.
Reframed around measurable burnup and retention under representative conditions.
Reframed as long-lived, low-intervention remote power with explicit oversight and end-of-life requirements.
Reframed as a durable material-and-chemistry system for specified coolant conditions.
Reframed as validated diagnosis with quantified uncertainty; control benefits need separate proof.
Reframed as substantially stronger, assessable resistance combined with safeguards.
The entry encompasses both approaches; the historical combination of high thrust and specific impulse, and the claimed Mars transit time, are not assumed.

reconciliation_change_log.change: Retained NUC-01 through NUC-05 and their distinct identities. Corrected the title of the 2025 IAEA report cited in the first pass and made access limitations explicit.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: The five first-pass concepts retain their IDs.

reconciliation_change_log.change: Added NUC-06 through NUC-13 for radiation-resistant materials, low-neutron fusion, passive safety, high-burnup fuel, remote-site power, coolant compatibility, core diagnosis, and proliferation resistance.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: Each describes a capability that could plausibly cross the requested impact threshold if demonstrated at useful scope.

reconciliation_change_log.change: Replaced historical absolutes with testable claims: no assumed immunity, perfect retention, universal safety, zero proliferation risk, or elimination of repositories. Removed unsupported fixed numerical targets as requirements.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: The historical absolutes and fixed requirements are not established in the research notes.

reconciliation_change_log.change: Flagged overlaps rather than merging concepts. NUC-07 in particular is a distinct fuel-cycle capability that also overlaps the general fusion-plant demonstration in NUC-01.
reconciliation_change_log.reason: The missing capabilities and demonstrations differ.
